Fairly dry conditions are expected over the Marianas for the next
couple of days. The exception will be Guam during the afternoon
Sunday and Monday, with the light winds and low cloud cover allowing
island convection both days, giving the island scattered showers and
a possible thunderstorms or two. By Tuesday, increasing convection
will spread over the islands as a weak disturbance approaches closer
to the Marianas as it heads toward the there are three main feature
affecting the region, first northern CNMI. By the end of next week, 
a dry pattern returns to the region and continues into the weekend.

Marine/Surf...
Not much going on in the marine or surf forecast. Light to gentle
winds will continue through the middle of next week, with seas of 3
to 5 feet building a bit toward the end of the week, reaching 5 to 7
feet. For now, most of the waters will see 3 to 4 foot swell. The
exception is the far eastern waters where altimetry is showing seas
of around 5 feet. Near the coast, however, swell should remain around
3 feet, producing a surf of 3 to 5 feet along east facing reefs,
resulting in a moderate risk of rip currents. All other reefs will
have a low risk of rip currents.

Tropical Systems...
A weak disturbance found along the monsoon trough, Invest 90W, is
centered east of the Marianas near 12N156E. Invest 90W is currently 
sub-low, meaning development is not expected for the next day or so. 
Analyses show mainly a weak, elongated circulation along the monsoon 
trough. Invest 90W looks to slowly move north-northwest over the next
few days, with little to no development for the next couple of days,
then slow strengthening as it continues NNW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A trough is moving into Majuro tonight and a there are three main
feature affecting the region, first a band of numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms is expected to develop over the island. 
Locally heavy showers are possible. Winds are light to gentle from 
the northwest so any storms that develop will be slow moving. This 
band of storms is expected to weaken sometime tomorrow morning, so 
shower coverage should return to scattered by the afternoon and 
continue through Monday. A brief dry period may occur before a new 
wave of moisture enters the region Tuesday. Seas of 6 feet tonight 
will decrease a foot or so tomorrow and remain steady.

Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will become isolated by
tomorrow for Kosrae, with a dry spell continuing for much of the
forecast period. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms may
return by Thursday. Seas will remain at 5 to 6 feet most of the 
forecast period.

Pohnpei's proximity to Invest 90W to the north-northwest will bring 
numerous locally heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms to the 
island tonight and tomorrow, with gusty winds possible. Seas will
also be elevated through at least tomorrow at 6 to 7 feet. As 90W
pushes to the north-northwest, dryer weather can be expected with
mostly isolated showers. Showers may be scattered Monday night and
Thursday with isolated thunderstorms possible.

Western Micronesia...
The Small Craft Advisory for Chuuk was allowed to expire.

There are two circulations embedded within the monsoon flow, the 
first, is located near 10N142E, to the east of Yap Proper, and 
Invest 90W mentioned above in the Tropical Systems Section. 

The first circulation is producing scattered showers along the
southwestern flank over Palau. This feature is expected to keep
scattered showers over Palau through the middle of next week. This
will provide some much needed rain to the region.

The Invest 90W is pulling a lot of moisture from south of the
Equator. This is producing showers along a convergence axis from 
EQ142E to 12N156E, passing over Chuuk lagoon. Satellite imagery shows
scattered showers along this axis, however, model guidance is 
showering widespread showers.

Altimetry shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet for much of Yap State. 
The primary swell for Palau and Yap is from the west, while the 
primary swell at Chuuk is from the south generated by a low-pressure
system south of the equator. Surf along south and west facing reefs
are expected to be elevated but below the 9 foot threshold for High
Surf Advisory. Winds near Palau are expected to be gentle to fresh, 
at Yap winds are expected to be light to moderate, and at Chuuk they 
are gentle to fresh.
